label: sprites/fw_steam.spr: a steam puff that rises and thins, animated

againstClass.words: starts too bright: an attack in its envelope
does not end dark: a decay in its envelope

R1.reason: The frame is one flat, hard-edged light-grey disc (the whole 32x32 frame, centre to edge). It is not a steam puff: no billowing or soft cloud edge, no rising or thinning. The image is the decoy's plain disc, so the effect the brief asks for is missing.

R2.reason: The frame is 32x32 as the measurements say, and the disc fills most of it with a border of 0. But the outline is a hard circle with no wisps or lobes, so it does not fill the frame the way a steam puff does. Clearly off.

R3.reason: A near-white grey reads plausibly as steam on the dark background, so the hue is roughly right by eye. It is one flat value across the whole disc, with no tonal variation or thinning, so it does not read as the blended colour of a puff. Clearly off.

R4.reason: Fails the class measures. The sprite has 1 frame, so it is not animated, and the brief asks for a rising, thinning puff. The envelope starts and ends at full brightness (first 1, last 1, peak at frame 0) against the smoke puff class's first 0 to 0.35, last 0 to 0.1 and peak 0.2 to 0.6. Nothing rises or thins.

R5.reason: Additive format and the file name fw_steam.spr read back as written. But the type is 'parallel' where the amendment of 2026-10-16 says the game's steam1 is 'parallel oriented'. Clearly off on type, so it is not a clean pass.
